title: Development of near-infrared spectroscopy for estimating organic matter in agricultural soil
author: Santasup, Theanjumpol, et al.

steps.title: Collect and prepare soil samples
steps.instruction: Collect 200 topsoil samples (0–20 cm depth) from agricultural fields in Chiang Mai Province using a composite auger method; transport to the laboratory, remove surface grass and plant debris, air‑dry the soils naturally, then pass each sample through a 0.5 mm mesh sieve before any chemical analysis.

steps.title: Determine organic matter by Walkley‑Black
steps.instruction: Oxidize organic carbon in each sieved soil sample with 0.167 M potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) solution in concentrated H₂SO₄, then back‑titrate the un‑reduced dichromate with ferrous sulfate using the o‑phenanthroline‑ferrous complex as indicator to calculate organic matter content.

steps.title: Measure total carbon by combustion
steps.instruction: Weigh exactly 0.05 g of each soil sample into a carbon‑free (C‑free) boat and analyse the sample in a C‑S Analyzer (Analytikjena) to obtain total carbon percentage.

steps.title: Measure total nitrogen by combustion
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.10–0.50 g of each soil sample, encapsulate the material in nitrogen‑free tin foil, and analyse it in an N‑Analyzer (LECO) to obtain total nitrogen percentage.

steps.title: Acquire near‑infrared spectra
steps.instruction: Record near‑infrared spectra of each prepared soil sample over the 800–2500 nm range (instrument details not specified in the source).

steps.title: Preprocess spectral data
steps.instruction: Apply three preprocessing methods separately to the raw spectra: (1) Savitzky–Golay smoothing, (2) Standard Normal Variate (SNV), and (3) Multiplicative Scatter Correction (MSC).

steps.title: Split data for calibration and validation
steps.instruction: Randomly assign 65 % of the soil samples to the calibration set and the remaining 35 % to the validation set for each preprocessing method.

steps.title: Develop PLS regression models
steps.instruction: For each preprocessing method, build partial least squares (PLS) regression models linking NIR absorbance to the reference values of organic matter, total carbon, and total nitrogen.

steps.title: Assess model performance
steps.instruction: Calculate the coefficient of determination (R²) and root‑mean‑square error (RMSE, %). The model with the highest R² and lowest RMSE is considered the best.

steps.title: Record calibration and validation statistics
steps.instruction:
Document the following statistics (Table 2):
- SOM: Raw spectral R² = 0.93, RMSE = 0.53 % (cal); R² = 0.83, RMSE = 0.62 % (val). Smoothing R² = 0.92, RMSE = 0.54 % (cal); R² = 0.84, RMSE = 0.618 % (val). SNV R² = 0.81, RMSE = 0.86 % (cal); R² = 0.58, RMSE = 0.992 % (val). MSC R² = 0.84, RMSE = 0.77 % (cal); R² = 0.66, RMSE = 0.895 % (val).
- Total carbon: Raw spectral R² = 0.93, RMSE = 0.274 % (cal); R² = 0.82, RMSE = 0.345 % (val). Smoothing R² = 0.92, RMSE = 0.292 % (cal); R² = 0.82, RMSE = 0.344 % (val). SNV R² = 0.81, RMSE = 0.446 % (cal); R² = 0.59, RMSE = 0.516 % (val). MSC R² = 0.84, RMSE = 0.398 % (cal); R² = 0.65, RMSE = 0.474 % (val).
- Total nitrogen: Raw spectral R² = 0.89, RMSE = 0.035 % (cal); R² = 0.56, RMSE = 0.067 % (val). Smoothing R² = 0.86, RMSE = 0.038 % (cal); R² = 0.57, RMSE = 0.066 % (val). SNV R² = 0.82, RMSE = 0.044 % (cal); R² = 0.44, RMSE = 0.075 % (val). MSC R² = 0.78, RMSE = 0.049 % (cal); R² = 0.50, RMSE = 0.071 % (val).

steps.title: Select best predictive models
steps.instruction: Choose the smoothing‑preprocessed PLS model as the best for organic matter (R² = 0.84, RMSE = 0.618 %) and total carbon (R² = 0.82, RMSE = 0.344 %). Note that nitrogen models did not achieve satisfactory prediction (validation R² = 0.44–0.57).
